# Audit154 — quantitative failure of proposed closure certificates

PROOF_AUDIT=PASS_WITHIN_SESSION
GLOBAL_BRIDGE=FAIL_FOR_TESTED_CERTIFICATES
EXTERNAL_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT=false
NEW_GLOBAL_OR_NEGLIGIBLE_SECTOR_BOUND=false
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0

## Three distinct populations, kept separate

The scalar set consists of products pq with distinct split primes in [T,2T], outside152's S_B, with B=4T^2. Its cardinality is asymptotic to a positive constant times B/(log B)^2. This is NOT a lower bound for physical endpoints.

The Gaussian norm-relation graph retains existence of nonzero cofactor C with p^2|Norm(C). It is a necessary relaxation. Its two directions can use different witnesses; neither mutual acceptance nor finite graph membership is a physical cuboid assertion.

The physical population retains the original canonical masks, positive primitive edges, face diagonals, same-witness reconstruction, sphere identity and exact R cutoff.153's reconstruction bounds this population from the necessary witnesses. No reverse implication is used.

## Certificate-cost theorem

For any alphabet S, k=|S intersect V_T|. Every covered semiprime pq contributes a positive term of at least1 to W_S(B,sigma), for EVERY sigma>0. Therefore inf_sigma W_S>=binom(k,2). The other cap C0*K^|S| also exceeds binom(k,2), since C0>=1 and K>=2. Taking their minimum is safe in the lower-bound direction. Covering every pair forces the sum of pair incidences to be at leastbinom(v,2), even with overlaps. This proves a lower bound on the NUMERIC UPPER CERTIFICATE, and hence its inability to certify the sufficient o(B^(1/3)) scale. It says nothing about a hypothetical improved physical cap or a cover of a separately proved sparse physical subset.

The polylog-alphabet family-size obstruction is secondary; the main theorem permits arbitrary alphabet sizes. This avoids claiming that a sufficient exponent budget is a necessary condition for every possible method.

## Bilateral peeling check

For prime q=1 modulo4, #H(q)=12. Three choices of a two-edge index set give3*12^2 witnesses, and the three-edge set gives12^3:2160 total. Norm(C)<=9q^4<=144T^4. Three distinct p>=T contributing squared prime divisors would force T^6<=144T^4, impossible when T>12. Thus at most2 candidates per witness,4320 encodings per q. The exponent is fixed at1 on squarefree R=pq.153's positive-edge reconstruction supplies at most one physical endpoint per full encoding.

Consequently the supplied bilateral fiber bounds yield O(T/log T), not the needed o(T^(2/3)) sufficient benchmark. A matching supplies an exact abstract countermodel to any implication from bounded degrees alone. It is expressly NOT a constructed arithmetic matching; no lower density of the actual graph is proved.

The shared-edge equality in(154.5) follows because both oriented H values reconstruct one edge and its complementary diagonal, differing only by conjugation. Its intersection index exists because two subsets of size at least2 in a three-element set intersect. This is a concrete compatibility condition to retain in future incidence estimates, not a claimed new saving.

## Geometric theorem applicability and height check

The cuboid equations are four monic square-root extensions of the edge-coordinate algebra. Over an algebraically closed field, each radicand has an odd branch component absent from the others; their squareclasses are independent. The generic extension is a field of degree16. Freeness of the monic presentation makes the coordinate algebra torsion-free over the base and injective into that generic field, proving geometric integrality. The resulting projective surface has codimension4 and degree2^4=16.

This is enough for Salberger's general Theorem0.9(b); smoothness or an embedding in P^3 is not needed. The theorem's degree-d curves/exceptions budgets were checked directly in the primary paper. Theorem0.5 for nonsingular surfaces in P^3 was not substituted. On every original positive primitive endpoint H=R exactly. Thus the supplied budgets are B^(3/8)log B and B^(3/4+o(1)), both above the benchmark. This is failure of the supplied bounds, not proof that no sharper cover exists.

Under a k-th Veronese embedding the surface degree is multiplied by k^2 and the exact height is raised to k. Primitive monomial coordinates have gcd1: a prime dividing all pure k-th powers would divide every original coordinate. The maximum monomial is R^k. Both B exponents therefore stay3/8 and3/4, respectively. Ignoring this height change would create spurious progress.

## Source verification and historical dedupe

-NIST DLMF27.11, final paragraph: the prime number theorem for a fixed coprime residue class. Used only for the scalar candidate and prime-window sizes. https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11
-Per Salberger, Counting rational points on projective varieties, Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society(2023), DOI10.1112/plms.12508, Theorem0.9(b). Used for the general surface curve/exception budgets. https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1112/plms.12508

Both were read from their primary publisher/official sources in this session. The degree/height adapter, cover-cap lower bound and graph inference audit are derived here. No literature-wide novelty is claimed.

HIST14-WITNESS-FW-001 already warns that finite witness fibers and balanced divisor windows do not prove density saving; this principle is credited, not rediscovered as a new theorem.151's scalar-support obstruction and150's coverage/residual firewall also remain in force. The added content is their quantitative application to the exact152/153 proposed bridge, plus the explicit geometric budget screen.

## Replay and interpretation

verify154.py uses standard-library exact integer and Fraction arithmetic. Verification154.json records596160 labelled Gaussian witness checks,16988 nonzero norm/window checks, eight windows T=13,32,...,2048,16 finite Euler-cap checks and100 Veronese exponent checks.

The mutual norm graph includes(13,17) in the T=13 window and no mutual pairs in the seven other tested windows. These finite observations are NOT extrapolated into an all-prime theorem or a cuboid nonexistence statement. They confirm that arithmetic correlations deserve analysis, while bounded-degree information alone is insufficient. Do not continue the census as a substitute for the needed uniform proof.

## Operational outcome

Retain152/153 unchanged. Stop automatic alphabet enlargement, repeated independent prime peeling, and degree-inflation as proposed closure mechanisms. T11 remains active with155=SameWitnessGlobalIncidenceBudget; the entire E_bal still needs a bound. Keep global credit0, gateOPEN, TIparked,120retracted,147–149retained. Proof-audit PASS and closure-bridge FAIL are deliberately separate statuses.

# M3-T11-153 — Proof and aggregate-budget audit

VERDICT=PASS_WITHIN_SESSION
REVIEW_MODE=WITHIN_SESSION_REDERIVATION_NOT_EXTERNAL_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW
PRIMARY_GATE_STATUS=OPEN
GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0
SECTOR_COUNTING_PROGRESS=true

## Claim audited

On the original primitive canonical positive endpoint population, at exact R<=B, let N(B,Y) count the union over ALL p^n||R with m=R/p^n<=Y. The proved bound is

 N(B,Y)<=512 Y(1+log Y)^27(1+log B),  B>=2, 1<=Y<=B.

This is an aggregate theorem, not a fixed-m or fixed-p estimate. Taking Y=B^(1/3)/(1+log B)^30 yields O(B^(1/3)/(1+log B)^2)=o(M3). It leaves the balanced residual defined in the research card unbounded.

## Load-bearing checks

1. Population bridge:151 already supplies an injection from original endpoints into primitive positive integer edge/complementary-diagonal data.153 does not replace this by a curve parameter population. Every qualifying endpoint has at least two p-unit edges. All primes ofR are split and at least5.

2. Orientation: one pi above each p is chosen deterministically. Independently conjugating each H_i preserves its real edge and moves its entire p^(2n) Gaussian factor onto bar(pi). The resulting cofactor G_i has norm m^2. Units are included in the full set H(m); there is no omitted sign/orientation packet.

3. Nonzero eliminant: C=sum G_i^2 cannot vanish for a positive endpoint. For r=2 vanishing forces the third edge to zero; for r=3 it contradicts R>0. Zero witnesses must be discarded BEFORE prime enumeration. Replay confirms the zero-edge boundary(0,3,4;R=5) has C=0, so this step is not a genericity assertion.

4. Prime cost: pi^2|C implies p^2|Norm(C), not merely p|Norm(C). For fixed witness, Norm(C) is a specific nonzero integer at most9m^4. Its distinct eligible primes cost at most log(9m^4)/(2log5). We drop the orientation-specific divisibility only to enlarge the candidate set. This is a deterministic integer-divisor budget, not a probability assigned to prime splitting or phases.

5. No inverse-multiplicity gap: specifying m,I,G_i,p,n determines the p-unit edges. With r=2 the missing positive edge is uniquely determined by the sphere equation. Its two signs are not both physical. Complementary face diagonals and the original canonical endpoint follow from the retained bridge. Nonintegral or invalid data contribute zero. There is no extra R^o(1) fiber factor and no hidden family cost. Multiple encodings only overcount safely; a least qualifying p selects an injection.

6. Exponents: sum all n>=1 satisfying mp^n<=B, at cost at most logB/log5. This handles the r=2 high-valuation branch; it does not import the stronger r=3 inequality into r=2.

7. Witness sum: if D(m)=product(2a+1), then 3(4D)^2+(4D)^3<=112D^3. The local inequality (2a+1)^3<=binom(a+26,26) follows by induction from the displayed polynomial ratio identity. Therefore D^3<=tau_27. The27-fold divisor sum is at mostY(1+logY)^26 by an elementary factor-tuple count. Extending split odd m to all m only enlarges the sum. The fixed absolute constant512 covers112*4/[2(log5)^2]<87 and replacement of logB by1+logB.

8. Residual accounting:152's small alphabet sector is assigned first;153's qualifying cofactor sector is assigned second outside it; the remainder has no small complementary factor. Thus the partition is disjoint, and no overlapping savings are multiplied. P_small and P_peel are both o(M3), making the full target equivalent to the still-unproved P_bal=o(M3).

9. Nonvacuity of the algebraic receiver versus existence: finite cofactor witnesses with nonzero C and candidate primes do occur (see JSON). They are NOT asserted to be physical cuboids. No existence or nonexistence of cuboids is inferred from the replay. On top dyadic shells,153's new nearly1/3-threshold sector is restricted by151 to r=2 and n>=2. This limitation is stated in the card; claiming removal of all large squarefree-prime mass would be false.

## Improvement over an initially looser proof

A first counting idea multiplied the witness count by the whole fixed-R Gaussian triple count R^o(1). Reconstructing the last positive edge removes that unnecessary factor. Charging D(m)^3 against tau_27 also replaces an unspecified m^o(1) sum by an explicit logarithmic cost. These corrections yield the nearly B^(1/3) threshold with a proved logarithmic saving. This is why the final result is more than another fixed-cofactor lemma.

## Dedupe and limits

151 contains the Gaussian divisibility and the failure of the scalar dominant-prime candidate sieve. It does not sum the nonzero cofactor witnesses.152 counts one prescribed prime alphabet and proves separate all-height finiteness. Neither estimates the union over unrestricted moving p via small m. COMMON-001, XD-001 and118/119 were checked in the live ledger: their populations and summation interfaces differ and are not imported here. Old Stage14 charged-cofactor work is not rebranded as this theorem. No claim of literature-wide novelty is made.

The elementary proof is self-contained once the audited151 endpoint bridge is retained. No new external theorem, unit-equation constant, PNT, determinant method or independence heuristic is needed. The application has a within-session audit, not an external independent hostile audit.

## Exact replay

verify153.py uses only the Python standard library. Recorded PASS checks:

-1001 local binomial/ratio-identity checks;
-exact divisor-sum majorants for seven cutoffs;
-67664 ordered Gaussian witness tuples over nine split cofactors, checking the nonzero norm bound and squared-prime budget;
-736 exact Gaussian orientation/reconstruction roundtrips;
-64 exponent-budget checks;
-the zero-edge C=0 counterexample;
-the logarithmic budget30-27-1=2.

These finite checks supplement the written uniform proof and exercise failure cases. They do not replace it. Verification153.json records the domains and examples.

## Durable continuation

Latest result153; next154=BalancedResidualJointGaussianCount. Prove a summed estimate for the residual with some prime outside S_B and R/p^v_p(R)>Y_B for every p|R. Preserve TI parked,120 retracted,147–149 retained and no automatic curve-degree escalation. Do not credit the full global gate or repeat the already-summed small-cofactor sector.

Handoff repair: direct fetch and exact-byte comparison recovered all four152 artifacts, including verify152.py (1WBlzhBdvCA-oyMhNJC6V_JJHW4GMy1vM) and verification152.json (1Q1gCTytRlm6xCxROlIb4477ZbCyiwA7I). The prior authority's NOT_CONFIRMED_BY_CURRENT_DRIVE_SEARCH statement is obsolete as an operational pointer; no mathematical result is retracted by this repair.

# Audit152 — weighted support sum, physical nondegeneracy and the residual budget

RESULT=WITHIN_SESSION_PROOF_AUDIT_PASS_WITH_EXPLICIT_RESIDUAL
EXTERNAL_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT=false
GLOBAL_GATE=OPEN

Authority read fresh: MAIN/INDEX/RESULT-LEDGER/active T11 ROUTE all151; full151 standalone card. Retained138's primitive ordered physical tuple, odd R and exact-height convention were checked in the ledger. Targeted comparison covered COMMON-001, XD-001, HIST14-GAUSS-FW-001,118/119 and the singular-carrier S-unit descent047/048. No whole-history reread or duplicated fixed-conductor theorem is used.

1. Exact equation. For Hi=ei+i fi, NormHi=R^2; zi=Hi^2/R^2=Hi/barHi has absolute value1. Its inverse is its conjugate. Summing real parts gives sum_i(zi+zi^-1)=2 sum_i(ei^2-fi^2)/R^2=-2. The6-variable equation has coefficients all-1/2 and right side1. Coefficients do not enlarge the multiplicative group's rank or require prime2 in S.

2. All63 degeneration cases are covered. Odd cardinality1/3/5: each real numerator ei^2-fi^2 is odd over common odd denominatorR^2, so a sum of odd cardinality is nonzero. Size2 same edge: R^2=2ei^2 is impossible in nonzero integers. Size2 different edges: real part zero forces ei^2+ej^2=R^2 and the remaining edge zero. Size4: complement consists of two unit complex numbers with sum-2, forcing both to be-1; a zi equal-1 has ei=0. Size6: sum-2. This proof handles conjugate choices and repeated numerical values, since subsets concern six indexed occurrences. No claim of generic nondegeneracy is substituted for proof.

3. Boundary audit. Primitive zero-edge triples(0,3,4),R=5 and(0,5,12),R=13 satisfy all circle/sphere equations with complementary faces(R,b,a), but have cancelling phase pairs. They verify that allowing zero edges would invalidate the application. They are not physical positives and are never charged to P(B). Exact replay checks a family of such examples, rather than pretending an empty search for perfect cuboids verifies the theorem.

4. Group rank. Because every Gaussian prime of Hi divides an integer prime dividingR, zi is supported above S. Norm-one valuations satisfy v_pi(z)+v_barpi(z)=0. Z[i] is a UFD; its units are finite. The quotient by torsion is free of rank|S|. The inverse-pair embedding G_S^3 -> (C*)^6 is injective and has rank3|S|. It is safe to enlarge from the even-valuation phase subgroup to all of G_S. Rank6|S| is a valid but unnecessarily weak ambient bound; rank|S| would be WRONG because the three phases have separate exponent vectors.

5. Published quantitative input. Amoroso–Viada, On the zeros of linear recurrence sequences, Acta Arith.147.4, DOI10.4064/aa147-4-4, publisher PDF https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/83761 . Page389, proof of Lemma2.1, states the bound(8n)^[4n^4(n+r+1)] from the authors' earlier Theorem6.2. Both parsed text and a screenshot of page389 were inspected. We use n=6,r=3|S|, so 4*6^4=5184 and the result is48^[5184(7+3|S|)]. This is not a linear-recurrence theorem misapplied to multidimensional exponents: the input is the explicitly stated multiplicative-group equation estimate. The same authors' own proof is a primary source. The earlier Duke5 PDF was inaccessible and was NOT claimed read. The weaker ESS Theorem1.1 was independently read in https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0409604, pp.807–808, as a fallback check of theorem type.

6. Physical inverse and measures. A zi coming from a physical point has a unique square root with positive real part, recovering Hi/R including the sign of fi. Ordered normalized edges fix a rational ray. If two positive primitive integer edge triples lie on it, a rational proportionality factor has denominator dividing the gcd of the first triple, hence is integral; primitivity of the second makes it1. R is then determined by the sphere equation. Canonical packet/source masks do not become additional labels to count; one endpoint remains one count. The count is uniform in all packet contents and includes isolated or positive-genus points. Nothing depends on147–149's parametrized-curve scope.

7. Important correction during this audit. The initial draft's growing-sector bound from the unit equation is mathematically valid but dominated by elementary smooth-support counting. It is NOT a counting gain requiring the deep theorem. The final card makes the stronger direct weighted sum the main sector result and retains the group bound as separate all-height uniform finiteness. Draft bytes were replaced in place before native authority promotion; file IDs remain unchanged.

8. Exact weighted summation. At R=product p^n, there are at most64 product(2n+1)^3 ordered Gaussian triples. For sigma>0,1_(R<=B)<=B^sigma/R^sigma. Summing independently over exponent vectors now computes an UPPER BOUND, not a probability model: the product of local series F(p^-sigma) is exactly their positive Dirichlet sum. F(x)=(1+23x+23x^2+x^3)/(1-x)^4 follows by applying(2x d/dx+1)^3 to1/(1-x). Thus P_S(B)<=64B^sigma product F(p^-sigma), with all exponent, unit and representation costs included. Original masks and the sphere equation can be dropped for this upper bound. No saving is multiplied by151 or by the unit-equation estimate; use the minimum.

9. Uniform alphabet-size estimate. For sigma in a compact subinterval of(0,1), logF(x)<=C_sigma x uniformly on[0,2^-sigma], with C_sigma bounded over that compact interval. The jth distinct prime is at least j+1; therefore sum_(p inS)p^-sigma<=sum_(j<=s)(j+1)^-sigma=O_sigma(s^(1-sigma)). With s<=(logB)^A,A>1 fixed, sigma=1-1/A+(loglogB)^-1/2 stays in such an interval for largeB. The product's logarithm is O(logB exp(-A sqrt(loglogB)))=o(logB), while the extra sigma exponent is o(1). This proves P_S(B)<=B^(1-1/A+o(1)), UNIFORMLY in the actual primes. At A=4/3 the exponent is1/4+o(1); any1<A<3/2 beats1/3. No prime number theorem, unproved density assumption or external deep theorem is needed for this sector result.

10. Residual and quantifiers. For the first floor((logB)^(4/3)) split primes S_B, the complement consists exactly of endpoints with some prime divisor ofR outsideS_B. Its mass is unbounded by this result. Eventual coverage of each fixed point is not uniform coverage at growing height. A family requires the complete sum of min(C0K^|S|,inf_sigma W_S(B,sigma)), and a complementary residual bound. If #F_B<=B^alpha and each |S|<=(logB)^A, uniformity gives exponent alpha+1-1/A+o(1); at A=4/3 require alpha<1/12. Replacing specified alphabets by arbitrary moving supports of cardinality<=s without paying for their choices is prohibited. No full P/M3 theorem, global power saving, or general nonexistence is obtained.

Decision: accept152's self-contained weighted support-sum theorem and growing-sector o(M3) bound; separately retain nondegeneracy and published-theorem-based all-height alphabet finiteness. Standard methods are not claimed novel. Keep global closure flags false. Next153 addresses the exact outside-alphabet residual or a support cover whose full cost is summable. TI remains parked;120 retracted;147–149 retained; automatic curve escalation remains stopped.

# Audit151 — dominant-prime necessary condition and rejected marginal bridge

Authority: fresh150 MAIN/INDEX/LEDGER/T11 ROUTE and full150 card. Focused ledger searches for dominant-prime/cofactor/prime-power-diagonal forms did not identify this exact bound. Existing Gaussian charged-block routes exist and must be checked before claiming152 improvements. No literature-wide novelty claim.

Proof checks:
1. Primitivity excludes inert primes in R; retained138 supplies odd R. At every split p|R, at most one edge is divisible by p, using the sphere equation modulo p. Thus r=2 or3, never1.
2. For p-unit e, H and its conjugate cannot both be divisible by pi. Conjugating each H independently permits v_pi(H)=0, v_bar(pi)(H)=2n. The sign of its imaginary part is irrelevant to H^2+bar(H)^2 and the sphere identity. Dividing by bar(pi)^(2n) leaves integral Gi of norm m^2. Gaussian units are included, not dropped.
3. For a p-divisible edge, both H and its conjugate are divisible by pi: modulo pi, i is a nonzero square root of minus1, and f is also p-divisible because e^2+f^2=R^2. Therefore each of their squares has valuation at least2. All conjugate p-unit terms have valuation4n. The integer2 is a pi-unit because p>=5. Hence pi^2|C for r=2, and v_pi(C)=2n for r=3. No transfer of curve-pole identities to integer prime factors occurs.
4. C=0 in r=2 forces the remaining edge zero through4e3^2=0; C=0 in r=3 contradicts2R^2=0. Neither case is permissible. Norm(C)<=r^2m^4 by the ordinary complex triangle inequality. Divisibility in Z[i] implies Norm(C)>=p^2, or p^(2n) for r=3. This proves p<=2m^2 or p^n<=3m^2, and the weaker all-endpoint p<=3m^2. No error term or unknown constant is used.
5. R prime power has m=1; p>=5 exceeds3, so excluded. This statement is about primitive positive cuboids, not all scaled/nonprimitive objects. ExactR<=B includes all excluded diagonal fibers with zero physical mass.
6. The relaxed-support witness uses q>5 split prime and k minimal with3*25^k>=q. Then5^k<5sqrt(q/3), and R(q)<5q^(3/2)/sqrt(3). For the5-factor,5^k<=3q^2; for q, q<=3*25^k. This witness passes even p^n<=3m^2 for every factor, stronger than the common necessary condition. Unique factorization recovers q, so no overlap correction is needed. PNT in progression1 mod4 (DLMF27.11, https://dlmf.nist.gov/27.11) gives at least constant B^(2/3)/log B candidates. None is asserted physical. This blocks only the scalar relaxed-support counting route, not the exact joint equation or the relative o(M3) goal.
7. For each split R, #H(R)=4 product(2n+1). All physical points inject into Gaussian triples obeying the exact sphere identity; signs/order may be fixed canonically, or safely enlarged for an upper bound. This receiver includes all genera and isolated points. The crude product-of-divisors bound is R^o(1) per R and B^(1+o(1)) in aggregate: NO saving. There is no residual claim concealed by a curve restriction.

Research decision: retain the integer-wide exclusion, reject its marginal support as a main counting attack, move152 only to averaged joint Gaussian-support correlation with exact physical height and explicit prime-allocation costs. Fixed-R bounds, independent local densities, finite searches and unlimited degree or prime-factor case enumeration are not acceptance criteria. GLOBAL_COUNTING_CREDIT=0; gateOPEN; TI parked;120 retracted.

Finite replay is supplemental: it verifies the exact Gaussian divisibility/norm implication on finite norm-m^2 tuples, the r=3 valuation-size implication, and every constructed relaxed support up to a stated prime limit. It cannot verify absent physical cuboids or replace the uniform proof. The replay has no positive physical examples and makes no existence inference.

# M3-T11-150 source/quantifier audit

Audit scope: whether138–149 establish a global counting bridge, not a re-audit/retraction of their mathematical proofs. Within-session source-grounded check, not external review.

Read current149 controls; actual GEOMETRY-CURVES route; current ledger CURVE-001/002/003/GATE-001. Confirmed: two-layer accumulating-family plus residual gate is old authority. Ledger002 already closes the fixed-model degree6 collective family contribution;003 retains negligibility for every fixed finite rational-degree band. These do not imply growing-degree or residual bounds. No comparison to138/139 parameter degree is assumed.

User correction accepted: full curve coverage is not necessary. A disjoint carrier/residual partition with both contributions o(M3(B)) suffices. o(B^(1/3)) is sufficient under the retained denominator lower bound, not a necessary rate. Union bounds allow overlap but require family summability; equality needs assignment.

Audit result: no quantitatively controlled decomposition/family cost/summed original-carrier contribution/residual estimate/high-complexity tail follows from138–149.149's two-root-pair theorem is universal in curve degree but its root-pair count is a parameter-map property, not an endpoint invariant. Arbitrary rational points/constant maps and positive-genus/nonsplit residuals remain. Even excluding all nonconstant rational curves would not alone count points. Fixed-degree versus moving-degree limit exchange is invalid; the toy moving-mass example is explicitly nonphysical.

Decision: curve-by-degree primary escalation STOPPED pending a genuine global bridge.147–149 retained, square-free sextic8000-pattern problem OPEN but not the default next attack.151 targets direct original eligible support or a summed carrier/residual estimate under exactR with packet/parameter cost and charging. No new count/exponent/nonexistence proof, no mathematical credit. Gate OPEN; TI parked;120 retracted. Latest numerical replay149 remains available; no150 numerical script is necessary for a source audit.

Readback requirement: save card/audit; update MAIN/INDEX/LEDGER/T11 ROUTE to150/next151/direct support; sync CARD-INDEX150 and its guide. Verify persisted contents before completion.

One maximal coordinate cannot cancel; two require sparse S vanishing twice and therefore identically zero, forcing the third edge zero; three require zero multiplicity2n>=4 while three sparse powers permit at most2, and an identically zero S leaves constant2.
